$comment: Authoritative contract for the Static Web App's runtime application settings.
WHY THIS IS A CONTRACT FILE AND NOT A BICEP RESOURCE:
Microsoft.Web/staticSites/config@... with name 'appsettings' REPLACES the entire
settings collection on every deploy. Declaring the eight non-secret values would
therefore DELETE the three secrets, and production would fail on the next apply:
no RESEND_API_KEY means the contact form answers 503, and no
CLASSIFY_QUEUE_SAS_URL means every lead enqueue throws. Declaring all eleven with
@secure() parameters is worse still — any deploy that forgot to pass them would
blank the secrets silently. So the settings stay operator-managed, and this file
makes the contract explicit and testable instead of tribal.
__tests__/infra/swa-settings.test.ts cross-checks this against the code's actual
process.env usage in both directions: a variable the code reads but nobody
provisions, and a setting provisioned that no code reads.
scripts/check-swa-settings.sh diffs this against the live resource (needs az).
Secret VALUES never appear here, and never should — this repo is public.

settings.name: RESEND_API_KEY
settings.note: Absent in preview environments by design; the handler surfaces 503 rather than throwing.

settings.name: CLASSIFY_QUEUE_SAS_URL
settings.note: Queue-scoped and add-only. Least privilege stands in for the managed identity the retired Functions app used.

settings.name: RESEND_TEST_MODE
settings.note: Legacy alias for EMAIL_TEST_MODE, still honoured.

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING
settings.note: NEXT_PUBLIC_, so it ships to the browser and is public by construction. Browser-side telemetry only — nothing server-side emits to App Insights.

settings.name: CONTACT_RATE_LIMIT_MAX
settings.sensitivity: anti-abuse tunable — value must not appear in this repo
settings.note: Anti-abuse tunable. Lives here and in the private runbook, never in code: a published rate limit tells someone exactly how to stay under it. The code default is deliberately stricter, so an unconfigured environment fails safe.

settings.name: CONTACT_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS
settings.sensitivity: anti-abuse tunable — value must not appear in this repo
settings.note: Anti-abuse tunable, window in milliseconds. Same reasoning as CONTACT_RATE_LIMIT_MAX.

notRuntimeSettings.$comment: Read by the code but supplied elsewhere, so absent from the SWA on purpose.

$comment: Azure Static Web Apps support @Microsoft.KeyVault() references ONLY for custom
authentication configuration. The MANAGED BACKEND that serves /api/* does not:
Microsoft's own documentation states that the serverless functions shipping with
Static Web Apps 'do not support direct Key Vault integration' and that Key Vault
access must be implemented in application code instead.
So setting RESEND_API_KEY to '@Microsoft.KeyVault(SecretUri=...)' would deliver
that LITERAL STRING to process.env at runtime. The Resend client would be
constructed with it as an API key and every send would fail — an outage of the
contact form, arrived at while trying to improve its security.
Tracking issues: Azure/static-web-apps#1090, #1091, #428.
Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/key-vault-secrets
THE ACTUAL CONTROLS for these three secrets, since Key Vault is not one:
- Azure RBAC on the Static Web App governs who can read app settings.
- CLASSIFY_QUEUE_SAS_URL is queue-scoped and add-only — least privilege by
construction, so a leak cannot read or delete messages.
- Rotation is the response to exposure, not removal.
- Values never enter this repository, in any form.
Do not reopen this as 'move the secrets to Key Vault'. The platform cannot do it.
